title: How to detect rented gig-worker accounts
summary: A $65 Facebook transaction is all it takes to put an unvetted stranger behind the wheel. Here's how Sixtyfour closes that gap.
body_markdown:
We use a single identifier (such as the account's phone number) to build a profile of the real owner, then compare it against operational signals like device ID and location to surface the likely renter's separate identity.


KYC is a one-time onboarding check. Continuous identity verification is the ongoing process of ensuring the person using the account is still the verified owner — on every session or transaction.


Platforms can detect suspicious internal signals like a new device or location, but they typically cannot see external data — breach records, dark web chatter — needed to confirm two different people are involved.


Our agents use an OSINT-based approach: take a known identifier, search across public records, social media, and breach databases, then resolve them into a single high-confidence identity graph.
